name: Facebook Sharing Debugger
title: Facebook Sharing Debugger: See What Facebook Scrapes
description: See what Facebook scrapes from your URL: we fetch it as facebookexternalhit, show the og: tags and image it uses, and explain how to force a re-scrape.
answer: A Facebook sharing debugger shows what Facebook's crawler sees when your link is shared. Enter a URL: we fetch it as facebookexternalhit, check the response and every og: tag Facebook uses, measure the image and render the Facebook card — no login needed.
trust: We request the page with the facebookexternalhit user agent, exactly as Meta's link-preview crawler identifies itself.
body:
## What does Facebook's crawler see?

Facebook builds previews with a crawler called facebookexternalhit. [Meta's documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/web-crawlers/) says it fetches pages shared in its apps to gather the title, description and thumbnail — and that it may bypass robots.txt for security or integrity checks.

This debugger sends a request with that user agent and shows the status code, redirects, every og: tag and the card Facebook would build from them.

## Facebook Debugger Tool: Why Your Old Image Still Shows

Facebook caches. [Meta says](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/images/) it caches images by URL, so replacing the file but keeping the same URL can leave the old picture in place. Two fixes:

1. Give the new image a new filename or a version query (`card.png?v=2`).
2. Ask Facebook to refresh: paste the page into Meta's official [Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/) and choose "Scrape Again".

Our tool shows what Facebook will see on its next scrape; Meta's tool is the one that clears Facebook's cache.

## Facebook Debug Tool Checklist: The og: Tags Facebook Needs

Four tags make a reliable Facebook card: og:title, og:description, og:image and og:url. Add og:image:width and og:image:height so the image renders on the first share. Meta recommends images of [at least 1200×630](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/images/), under 8 MB.

## Why does Facebook show no preview at all?

Usually the crawler can't get the page. Firewalls and bot protection often challenge facebookexternalhit, and a page that returns 403 or a challenge gives Facebook nothing to work with.

We saw how common that wall is when we fetched 391 well-known homepages with a labelled research crawler in October 2026 ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)): 55 answered with a 403. If your firewall blocks unknown crawlers, allow Meta's crawler explicitly.

Compare the Facebook card with five other platforms in the [link preview tool](/tools/link-preview), or check the image alone with the [OG image checker](/tools/og-image-checker).

faqs.q: How do I clear Facebook's cache for my link?
faqs.a: Paste the URL into Meta's Sharing Debugger at developers.facebook.com/tools/debug and click "Scrape Again". If the image still doesn't change, give the image file a new URL.

faqs.q: Do I need to log in to use this debugger?
faqs.a: No. We fetch your page as Facebook's crawler and show the result without any account. Only clearing Facebook's own cache requires Meta's tool and a login.
Meta says it may bypass robots.txt when performing security or integrity checks. To stop previews entirely, you would need to block it at the server or firewall.
